egui 0.36.2 from crates.io, with a selection highlight for right-to-left rows.

Why
egui 0.36.2 draws a selection as one rectangle per row, from the caret at
one end to the caret at the other. With the right-to-left layout in
vendor/epaint, the chars between two carets on a row with Arabic in it are
not always one stretch of the row. On a row that mixes directions, and on
the first and last rows of a selection over several right-to-left rows,
the rectangle covered the wrong part, and selected letters outside it
turned ink on the panel colour and all but disappeared. A two-row Arabic
message selected whole showed no highlight at all. Copy was right in
every case. This folder is 0.36.2 with its selection painter changed,
used through [patch.crates-io] in the workspace Cargo.toml. Drop the
folder and the patch line once an egui release paints selections on
bidi text, which will be the release that lays it out (vendor/epaint).

Where it comes from
The egui-0.36.2.crate in the local cargo cache, no download. Its SHA-256,
dc938cc27cd911415e1e4d151bc56ff9df063d8db081374e87aeb805ea74b2ba, is the
checksum Booth's Cargo.lock had for egui 0.36.2 before the patch. Cargo.lock,
.cargo_vcs_info.json and .cargo-ok left out.

Changed in src/text_selection/visuals.rs
- A row with a right-to-left glyph gets one rectangle per run of selected
  glyphs that sit next to each other on the row, the glyphs chosen by char
  index and walked in x order. A glyph that takes no room, a mark or the
  rest of a cluster, is drawn over the one before it and neither starts
  nor splits a run. A mark selected without its letter, which only the
  keyboard can do, highlights its letter's place: the mark turns the
  selected text colour like any selected char and would vanish on the
  bare panel.
- A run ends where the next glyph on the row starts. Glyphs sit on whole
  pixels and their advances are not whole, so ending it at the last
  glyph's own advance would reach up to a pixel into its neighbour, or
  leave a hairline before it.
- Every selected glyph on such a row gets the selected text colour by its
  own vertices, from its first vertex to the next glyph's.
- A newline selected after such a row shows as in 0.36.2, half the row's
  height wide, but at the end its paragraph reads towards: on the left of
  a right-to-left paragraph. That end is where the row's letters end on
  that side, not the row's width: while the vendored epaint gave a
  right-to-left row with vowel marks a width short of its letters, a
  newline put there landed on an unselected word. The paragraph's
  direction is the lowest bidi level among its glyphs, which its first
  strong letter has, and so does the whitespace at the end of each of its
  rows (UAX #9 rule L1); the vendored epaint does not keep the paragraph
  level itself. A paragraph with an explicit embedding around all of it
  can come out the wrong way, which only the composer can show.
- Such a row with nothing on it selected gets no rectangle, where 0.36.2
  added one with no width.
- Rows with no right-to-left glyph keep 0.36.2's code: one rectangle from
  caret to caret, the colour over the chars between them. The part that
  puts a rectangle into a row's mesh behind its glyphs moved, unchanged,
  into a function that both kinds of row use. That keeps 0.36.2's slip on
  a right-aligned row that starts with a space, which the layout hangs
  left of the row: the space stays out of the highlight, and a selection
  that ends where that row starts lays a sliver over it.
- An empty selection, the cursor and the IME underlines are as in 0.36.2.

Changed in src/text_selection/text_cursor_state.rs
- ccursor_previous_word clamps the cursor to the text's char count before
  taking it from the end. A letter IBM Plex Sans builds from two glyphs,
  such as U+01E9, gives the galley one more cursor place than the text
  has chars, and a double click or Ctrl+Left there underflowed, which a
  debug build stops on.
- ccursor_next_word never returns a place behind the cursor. From that same
  place past the end it gave the text's char count: Ctrl+Delete or Alt+Delete
  then asked for a backward range, whose assert in delete_char_range stops
  every build, and Ctrl+Right stepped back. Now Ctrl+Delete deletes nothing,
  Ctrl+Right stays, and a double click there selects up to the cursor, so
  the highlight reaches the end of the word.
- select_word_at leaves a plain caret on an empty last row. It has no word,
  and from that same place the selection would hold only the newline above,
  so copying it would put an empty string on the clipboard.
- Three tests for it, and one more in src/widgets/text_edit/text_buffer.rs.

Changed in src/text_selection/accesskit_text.rs
- 0.36.2 gives a text run's positions from its first glyph and calls them
  left to right. The first glyph of a right-to-left row is its rightmost, so
  every other position came out negative, and a magnifier or a screen
  reader's highlight was sent left of the row. Now a row all right to left
  says so and gives each caret place counted from the row's right end, as
  AccessKit reads them.
- A row of both directions gets no positions or widths, which AccessKit
  allows: it then gives no box for any range that touches the row, and most
  text functions still work. One text run per direction is what would give
  it boxes.
- The runs a row longer than 255 chars is cut into: on a row all right to
  left each one's bounds hold its own letters; on a row of both directions
  each one's bounds are the whole row, since its chars need not be one
  stretch of it. Before, the left end could come out past the right.
- Rows with no right-to-left glyph are as in 0.36.2.

Other changes to the crate
- Ten doc examples marked ignore. They include images by paths inside
  egui's own repository (assets/ferris.png, and eframe/data/icon.png),
  which the published crate does not carry; 0.36.2 already marks one more
  the same way.
- No dev-dependencies to remove: the published 0.36.2 has none.
- Everything else is as upstream wrote it, its TODO lines included.

LICENSE-MIT and LICENSE-APACHE are copies of vendor/epaint's, which are
egui's from github.com/emilk/egui at tag 0.36.2. Both crates' manifests
name the same two files at the root of that repository, and neither
published crate carries them, so the texts are the same.

Tests: cargo test -p egui --locked, from the workspace root, runs the
crate's own tests. The highlight is tested on Booth's fonts in
crates/app/src/screens/chat/bidi_tests.rs (cargo test -p app --locked):
inside an Arabic row, on mixed rows, from an Arabic row into an English
one, over two Arabic rows, a newline after Arabic with vowel marks, a mark
selected without its letter, in the composer, any selection of the
property test's texts, and against a copy of 0.36.2's painter, unchanged
but for its name and with its comments left out, which every row with no
right-to-left glyph must still match. The word keys past the last char are
tested there too, in the composer, and the positions AccessKit is given.
